This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hurst. The Army has detonated nearly five tons of unstable toxic material containing lead
stockpiled for nearly 20 years in Iowa. Video showed the blast sending a plume of smoke into the air.
Residents are worried about the effects of the possibly toxic lead dust cloud on people, animals, and crops.
The White House is proposing additional tariffs on goods from 13 countries and the EU,
framing the tariffs as responses to other countries' unfair trading practices. And Piers Daniel Kurtzleben has more.
The new tariffs would be on some of the US's largest trading partners, including China and the EU.
The administration says these are proposed tariffs and that they are seeking public comment on the new rates.
For each country, the administration has a proposed tariff rate and what the administration calls a deal rate,
a lower rate that they could be willing to impose.
A senior administration official told reporters Tuesday night that the tariffs on Chinese goods would be 20 percent,
but could go as high as 40 percent, depending on ongoing negotiations.
The new rates come just weeks after Republicans lost dozens of seats in Congress due in part to high prices, which tariffs can exacerbate.
Daniel Kurtzleben, NPR News.
Two Libyan naval officers have died of injuries sustained in the Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in eastern Libya earlier this week.
And Piers Joanna Kikisas has more.
The self-styled Libyan National Army revealed the news of the deaths in a statement late Tuesday.
The army's general vowed to take revenge at, quote, "the appropriate time and place and by the appropriate means."
The Libyan National Army has close ties to the Kremlin and is the most powerful group in a country divided by years of civil war.
Russia strikes Ukraine every day.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said this weekend that his country is striking back.
We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack.
He said Ukraine's military deployed seven sea drones to hit the Russian warship.
Joanna Kikisas, NPR News.
Saudi Arabia says nearly a dozen were wounded yesterday when Houthi rebels attacked a high rise in the capital's financial district and Piers Aya Batrawi has more.
Saudi Arabia's emergency rescue service posted a photo online showing several floors of the skyscraper damaged.
It says 11 people were wounded in this latest attack, among them Saudis, Egyptians, Indians and Nepalese.
Saudi Arabia blamed the attack on the Iran-backed Houthis who are targeting Saudi oil sites, airports and Riyadh's financial district with missiles and drones.
The Houthis say they also struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in Rastanurah in the east, sparking fires there.
The kingdom has yet to comment. Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The recent meta settlement requires the company to make an array of changes to its social media platforms.
But a new study finds that the impact of these changes on teen mental health will be limited if other social media platforms like Snapchat, YouTube and TikTok don't follow suit.
And Piers Ritu Chatterjee has more.
Smartphone data of 1,800 teenagers over nearly five years revealed that meta accounted for only 20 percent of all social media use across five platforms, including TikTok and YouTube.
Pediatrician Dr. Demetri Christakis is at Seattle Children's Hospital and an author of the new study published in JAMA.
He says a two hour limit on social media as required by the meta settlement would only affect 8 percent of teens.
Whereas if it were all five platforms, it would affect almost two thirds of teens.
Similarly, a midnight to 6 a.m. block on social media would affect 78 percent of meta users.
Ritu Chatterjee and PR News.
The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation guide rose last month.
The Commerce Department says its personal consumption expenditures price index showed a seasonally adjusted 3.8 percent inflation rate for the 12 months ending in October.
That's nearly twice the central bank's goal.
And the Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates at its meeting next month.
Wall Street sharply lower at this hour.
The Dow down 743 points.
That's one and a half percent drop.
The Nasdaq is down 982 points.
That's down 4.1 percent.
S&P 500 down 197 points.
